correctness.rationale: Pointwise Cauchy brightness formula yields A=max(2s,4a) and exact 3-vs-4 region split. Eight spherical triangle cones and 24 coordinate-dominant cones supply disjoint exhaustive Haar sectors. Two explicit azimuth-length integrations and their Jacobians yield both normalized densities; their positive lengths agree at the break. Analytic cone solid angles prove the event probabilities; all density moment identities match independent established results. A bundled independent planar hull checker validated 2,500 random projections and numerical integrations match p and the first two moments. Finite checks are corroborative and do not replace the coarea proof.

originality.rationale: The genuinely assessed claim is the entire type-resolved regular-tetrahedron area distribution, and exact positive-length constant posterior. Original unconditional area density (Vickers–Brown 2001), unweighted silhouette probabilities (Feldman–Klain and Finch), and arbitrary-tetrahedron first two conditional moments (2026 published finding) are expressly excluded from the novelty claim. Inspected primary texts do not state or imply both separate density measures from their reported results without additional cone-specific coarea integration. The 2001 cap approach makes implicit/independently known rediscovery a residual risk.
residual_risks: Historical priority is provisional; an unindexed type-resolved calculation may exist.
The 2001 Appendix B viewing-sphere cap computation supplies a potential route to the type-resolved density, though it does not state the joint distribution.
The 2015 particle-shape study was available only in extended excerpt form, not all embedded figures, and is not decisive coverage.
No independent external mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The complete joint density of area and silhouette combinatorics is a natural intrinsic statistic for a basic Euclidean polytope. Prior unconditional densities and a finite number of conditional moments cannot answer the area-conditional classification problem. The exact nonempty posterior plateau and sharp exclusion beyond the triangular support give geometric structure rather than a routine isolated scalar evaluation. It is not claimed to solve arbitrary-polytope shadow inference.
